entities.blurb: A stripped log or stripped stem is a variant of the log and stem, obtained by using an axe on a log or a stem respectively. Once stripped, it cannot be reversed.
entities.name: Stripped Oak Log

entities.blurb: Stripped wood or stripped hyphae is a variant of wood obtained when any axe is used on wood or hyphae respectively.
entities.name: Stripped Oak Wood

entities.blurb: A stripped log or stripped stem is a variant of the log and stem, obtained by using an axe on a log or a stem respectively. Once stripped, it cannot be reversed.
entities.name: Stripped Pale Oak Log

entities.blurb: Stripped wood or stripped hyphae is a variant of wood obtained when any axe is used on wood or hyphae respectively.
entities.name: Stripped Pale Oak Wood

entities.name: Stripped Spruce Log

entities.blurb: Stripped wood or stripped hyphae is a variant of wood obtained when any axe is used on wood or hyphae respectively.
entities.name: Stripped Spruce Wood

entities.blurb: Stripped wood or stripped hyphae is a variant of wood obtained when any axe is used on wood or hyphae respectively.
entities.name: Stripped Warped Hyphae

entities.blurb: A stripped log or stripped stem is a variant of the log and stem, obtained by using an axe on a log or a stem respectively. Once stripped, it cannot be reversed.
entities.name: Stripped Warped Stem

entities.blurb: A structure block is used to generate structures manually. They can also be used to save and load structures, alongside structure void blocks.
entities.name: Structure Block

entities.blurb: A structure void is an invisible block that is not saved by structure blocks, allowing for the creation of structures that leave some existing blocks unchanged when loaded in a different location.
entities.name: Structure Void

entities.blurb: Sugar cane is a plant that can only be placed on plantable blocks adjacent to water. It grows up to three blocks tall over time, but will instead uproot itself if its water is removed. Sugar cane can be crafted into sugar and paper.
entities.name: Sugar Cane

entities.blurb: Sulfur is a block that naturally generates in sulfur caves alongside cinnabar, in sulfur pools, and as part of sulfur springs.
entities.name: Sulfur

entities.blurb: A sulfur brick slab is a decorative slab variant of sulfur bricks.
entities.name: Sulfur Brick Slab

entities.blurb: Sulfur brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of sulfur bricks.
entities.name: Sulfur Brick Stairs

entities.blurb: A sulfur brick wall is a decorative wall variant of sulfur bricks.
entities.name: Sulfur Brick Wall

entities.blurb: Sulfur bricks are a decorative brick variant of sulfur.
entities.name: Sulfur Bricks

entities.blurb: A sulfur slab is a decorative slab variant of sulfur.
entities.name: Sulfur Slab

entities.blurb:
Sulfur spikes are blocks found in sulfur caves that form stalactites and stalagmites.
Stalactites (which point downward) grow over time when attached from underneath sulfur and can serve as falling projectiles, similar to dripstone.
Stalagmites (which point upward) do not deal extra fall damage, unlike pointed dripstone.
entities.name: Sulfur Spike

entities.blurb: Sulfur stairs are a decorative stairs variant of sulfur used for building.
entities.name: Sulfur Stairs

entities.blurb: A sulfur wall is a decorative wall variant of sulfur used for building.
entities.name: Sulfur Wall

entities.blurb: A sunflower is a tall flower that generates exclusively in sunflower plains biomes. It can be crafted into two yellow dye.
entities.name: Sunflower

entities.blurb: Suspicious gravel is a fragile gravity-affected block found in various Overworld structures. It can be brushed to extract unique structure-dependent loot from it. It drops nothing if it breaks, and breaks if it falls or is moved.
entities.name: Suspicious Gravel

entities.blurb: Suspicious sand is a fragile gravity-affected block found in various Overworld structures. It can be brushed to extract unique structure-dependent loot from it. It drops nothing if it breaks, and will break if it falls or is moved.
entities.name: Suspicious Sand

entities.blurb:
Sweet berries are a food item obtained from sweet berry bushes and are used to plant them.
Sweet berry bushes are quick-growing plants that grow sweet berries. Players and most mobs are slowed down and take constant damage while moving through them. They can be found naturally in taigas and snowy taigas.
entities.name: Sweet Berry Bush

entities.blurb: Tall dry grass is the tall variant of dry grass. Unlike other tall variants of foliage, this block is only one-block tall. It generates frequently in deserts and all types of badlands, and looks like a more full version of short dry grass. It also grows on sand and terracotta, and can be eaten by sheep.
entities.name: Tall Dry Grass

entities.blurb: Tall grass is the 2-block tall variant of short grass.
entities.name: Tall Grass

entities.blurb:
Seagrass is a non-solid plant block that generates underwater in most aquatic biomes.
Tall seagrass is a two-block high variety of seagrass.
entities.name: Tall Seagrass

entities.blurb: A target is a block that produces a temporary redstone signal when hit by a projectile. Unlike most other conductive blocks, it also redirects adjacent redstone dust toward it.
entities.name: Target

entities.blurb: Terracotta is a block that is found abundantly in badlands biomes, or can be obtained by smelting clay. It can be dyed to create stained terracotta.
entities.name: Terracotta

entities.blurb: A test block is a technical block that is used for game tests.
entities.name: Test Block

entities.blurb: A test instance block is a technical block that is used for game tests.
entities.name: Test Instance Block

entities.blurb: Tinted glass is a non-solid block that blocks light while being visually transparent.
entities.name: Tinted Glass

entities.blurb:
TNT is an explosive block that can be lit by a redstone signal, flint and steel, stray fire, flaming projectile or explosion.
When lit, TNT becomes primed TNT, a gravity-affected entity that produces a damaging, block-destroying explosion, usually after four seconds. Blocks destroyed by TNT always drop their usual items as if mined by a player.
entities.name: TNT

entities.blurb: Torches are non-solid blocks that emit light.
entities.name: Torch

entities.blurb: A torchflower is an ancient flower obtained from harvesting torchflower seeds. It can be crafted into orange dye.
entities.name: Torchflower

entities.blurb: Torchflower seeds are ancient seeds that have a chance to be dropped by sniffers when they finish digging. It is the seed of torchflowers.
entities.name: Torchflower Crop

entities.blurb:
A trapped chest is a type of chest that functions identically to its base counterpart, but has a red-tinted latch and produces redstone power while open.
Like normal chests, two trapped chests can merge into a large trapped chest if placed next to each other.
entities.name: Trapped Chest

entities.blurb:
A trial spawner is a type of spawner found in trial chambers. It spawns mobs in waves, ejects consumable items and/or trial keys after they are all defeated, and then deactivates for 30 minutes. Having more Survival/Adventure mode players nearby results in more mobs and more rewards.
A trial spawner will convert into an active ominous trial spawner during an ominous trial, even if it was on cooldown.
entities.name: Trial Spawner

entities.blurb: String is an item that can be used as a crafting material or placed as a tripwire to allow tripwire hooks and observers to detect entities that touch it.
entities.name: Tripwire

entities.blurb: A tripwire hook is a block used to create a tripwire circuit, which requires two hooks and a straight horizontal line of 1-40 string. Both hooks in a valid circuit emit a redstone signal and power their attached blocks while any of the string is being touched by an entity, or if any string is broken without using shears.
entities.name: Tripwire Hook

entities.blurb: Coral is a type of non-solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn. Each of them are vibrant and colorful, but turn gray when they die.
entities.name: Tube Coral

entities.blurb: A coral block is a solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Tube Coral Block

entities.blurb: Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Tube Coral Fan

entities.blurb: Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Tube Coral Wall Fan

entities.blurb: Tuff is an ornamental rock, occurring in underground ore blobs below Y=0 and as part of sulfur springs.
entities.name: Tuff

entities.blurb: A tuff brick slab is a decorative slab variant of tuff bricks that does not generate naturally and is commonly used for building.
entities.name: Tuff Brick Slab

entities.blurb: Tuff brick stairs are a decorative stairs variant of tuff bricks that do not generate naturally and are used for building.
entities.name: Tuff Brick Stairs

entities.blurb: A tuff brick wall is a decorative wall variant of tuff bricks that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: Tuff Brick Wall

entities.blurb: Tuff bricks are a brick variant of tuff found abundantly in trial chambers.
entities.name: Tuff Bricks

entities.blurb: A tuff slab is a decorative slab variant of tuff that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: Tuff Slab

entities.blurb: Tuff stairs are a decorative stairs variant of tuff used for building.
entities.name: Tuff Stairs

entities.blurb: A tuff wall is a decorative wall variant of tuff that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: Tuff Wall

entities.blurb: A turtle egg is a block that can be placed up to four times within one block space that hatches turtles.
entities.name: Turtle Egg

entities.blurb: Twisting vines are climbable upward-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in warped forests.
entities.name: Twisting Vines

entities.blurb: Twisting vines are climbable upward-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in warped forests.
entities.name: Twisting Vines Plant

entities.blurb: A vault is a block found in trial chambers that ejects loot when unlocked using a trial key. Each vault can be opened by an unlimited number of players, but each player can unlock a specific vault only once.
entities.name: Vault

entities.blurb: A froglight is a light-emitting block that is obtained when a frog eats a tiny magma cube. It comes in three variants based on the variant of frog that eats the magma cube.
entities.name: Verdant Froglight

entities.blurb: Vines are climbable non-solid vegetation blocks that grow on walls.
entities.name: Vines

entities.blurb:
Air is an invisible block used to define unoccupied space where other blocks and items could exist; it represents the absence of a block or an item. It is one of the few blocks in the game that players cannot normally interact with.
Cave air‌[Java Edition  only] is a variant found only underground in carver caves[verify for Java Edition] and some generated structures along with features like lava lakes.
Void air‌[Java Edition  only] is a variant used internally for the 'air' in unloaded chunks and outside of the world height limits (above Y=319 and below Y=-64 in the Overworld, and above Y=255 and below Y=0 in the Nether and the End dimensions).
entities.name: Void Air

entities.blurb: Torches are non-solid blocks that emit light.
entities.name: Wall Torch

entities.blurb: A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
entities.name: Warped Button

entities.blurb: The wooden door is a variant of the door made of wood that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Warped Door

entities.blurb: A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
entities.name: Warped Fence

entities.blurb: A fence gate is a block that shares the functions of both the door and the fence.
entities.name: Warped Fence Gate

entities.blurb: A warped fungus is a fungus found in warped and crimson forests or by using bone meal on nylium. It can grow into a huge warped fungus if bone mealed, but only if planted on warped nylium. It can also be used for crafting, fed to striders or be planted to repel hoglins.
entities.name: Warped Fungus

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Warped Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 11 types (12 in Third Drop 2026​[upcoming]): oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, pale oak, and poplar​[upcoming].
entities.name: Warped Hyphae

entities.blurb: Warped nylium is a variant of netherrack that generates in the Nether.
entities.name: Warped Nylium

entities.blurb: Planks are common blocks used as building blocks and in crafting recipes. They are usually one of the first things that a player crafts in Survival mode. There are currently 12​[until: Third Drop 2026]/13​[upcoming: Third Drop 2026] variants of planks, which can be differentiated into three categories: Overworld planks made from tree logs, bamboo planks made from blocks of bamboo, and nonflammable Nether planks made from huge fungus stems.
entities.name: Warped Planks

entities.blurb: A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
entities.name: Warped Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: Warped roots are a non-solid "plant" block which generate naturally on warped nylium and soul soil in warped forests. They resemble a colony of tall, thin mushrooms.
entities.name: Warped Roots

entities.blurb:
A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. Using an item slot exchanges its contents with the player's hotbar. Powering a shelf combines its three slots together and makes using it swap everything at once.
Two or three adjacent shelves can merge their slots together if all are powered, which allows for swapping six or nine items at a time, respectively.
entities.name: Warped Shelf

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Warped Sign

entities.blurb: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
entities.name: Warped Slab

entities.blurb: Wooden stairs are a wooden variant of stairs, crafted from their respective planks.
entities.name: Warped Stairs

entities.blurb: A log or stem is a naturally occurring block found in trees or huge fungi, primarily used as a building block and to create planks, a versatile crafting ingredient. There are currently nine types of logs: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, and pale oak; and two types of stems: crimson and warped. The upcoming third drop of 2026 introduces poplar as the tenth log type.
entities.name: Warped Stem

entities.blurb: A wooden trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Warped Trapdoor

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Warped Wall Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Warped Wall Sign

entities.blurb: Warped wart blocks are a decorative block found in warped forests, generating as part of huge warped fungus.
entities.name: Warped Wart Block

entities.blurb: Water is a fluid that naturally generates abundantly in the Overworld.
entities.name: Water

entities.blurb: A cauldron is a block that can contain water, lava, or powder snow and, in certain situations, collect them from the environment. In Bedrock Edition, it can also hold dyed water or potions and can be used to efficiently create tipped arrows. It also serves as a leatherworker's job site block.
entities.name: Water Cauldron

entities.blurb: Chiseled copper is a variant of copper blocks that generates in trial chambers.
entities.name: Waxed Chiseled Copper

entities.blurb: Copper bars are copper variants of bars. Unlike iron bars, they are colored copper orange and can oxidize over time, similar to other copper blocks.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Bars

entities.blurb: A block of copper, internally known as a copper block, is a block that oxidizes over time, gaining a verdigris appearance over four stages. They can be prevented from oxidizing by being waxed with honeycombs. Non-oxidized blocks of copper are storage blocks equivalent to nine copper ingots.
entities.name: Waxed Block of Copper

entities.blurb:
A copper bulb is a light-emitting block. It toggles on or off when it receives a redstone pulse, and does not need continuous power to emit light. Its light level depends on its state of oxidation.
Waxed copper bulbs do not oxidize, but otherwise function identically.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Bulb

entities.blurb: A copper chain is an oxidizing directional block and the copper variant of chains.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Chain

entities.blurb:
A copper chest is a type of chest made of copper. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it oxidizes over time, and copper golems remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests.
Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a large copper chest if placed adjacent each other.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Chest

entities.blurb: The copper door is a type of door made of copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Door

entities.blurb: A copper golem statue is the result of a copper golem fully oxidizing and petrifying into a block. It can be posed in four different ways, or it can be reanimated by scraping it with an axe enough times.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Golem Statue

entities.blurb: Copper grates are a variant of copper blocks that have perforations that can be seen through.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Grate

entities.blurb: A copper lantern is a copper variant of a lantern that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Lantern

entities.blurb: A copper trapdoor is a type of trapdoor made from copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone. A copper trapdoor can exist in one of eight variants depending on how oxidized it is and whether it is waxed or not.
entities.name: Waxed Copper Trapdoor

entities.blurb: Cut copper is an oxidizing metal block crafted from blocks of copper. Like other copper blocks, cut copper can be waxed to prevent oxidation.
entities.name: Waxed Cut Copper

entities.blurb: A cut copper slab is a decorative slab variant of cut copper that generates in trial chambers and is used for building. Unlike other types of slabs, cut copper slabs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Waxed Cut Copper Slab

entities.blurb: A cut copper slab is a decorative slab variant of cut copper that generates in trial chambers and is used for building. Unlike other types of slabs, cut copper slabs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Waxed Weathered Cut Copper Slab

entities.blurb: Cut copper stairs are a decorative stairs variant of cut copper that generate in trial chambers and are used for building. Unlike other types of stairs, cut copper stairs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Waxed Weathered Cut Copper Stairs

entities.blurb: A lightning rod is a block that, with sky access, causes natural lightning strikes in a large area to only target itself. Getting struck by lightning causes it to emit a redstone signal and, if it is not waxed, also reduces its level of oxidation.
entities.name: Waxed Weathered Lightning Rod

entities.blurb: Chiseled copper is a variant of copper blocks that generates in trial chambers.
entities.name: Weathered Chiseled Copper

entities.blurb: A block of copper, internally known as a copper block, is a block that oxidizes over time, gaining a verdigris appearance over four stages. They can be prevented from oxidizing by being waxed with honeycombs. Non-oxidized blocks of copper are storage blocks equivalent to nine copper ingots.
entities.name: Weathered Copper

entities.blurb: Copper bars are copper variants of bars. Unlike iron bars, they are colored copper orange and can oxidize over time, similar to other copper blocks.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Bars

entities.blurb:
A copper bulb is a light-emitting block. It toggles on or off when it receives a redstone pulse, and does not need continuous power to emit light. Its light level depends on its state of oxidation.
Waxed copper bulbs do not oxidize, but otherwise function identically.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Bulb

entities.blurb: A copper chain is an oxidizing directional block and the copper variant of chains.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Chain

entities.blurb:
A copper chest is a type of chest made of copper. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it oxidizes over time, and copper golems remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests.
Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a large copper chest if placed adjacent each other.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Chest

entities.blurb: The copper door is a type of door made of copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Door

entities.blurb: A copper golem statue is the result of a copper golem fully oxidizing and petrifying into a block. It can be posed in four different ways, or it can be reanimated by scraping it with an axe enough times.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Golem Statue

entities.blurb: Copper grates are a variant of copper blocks that have perforations that can be seen through.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Grate

entities.blurb: A copper lantern is a copper variant of a lantern that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Lantern

entities.blurb: A copper trapdoor is a type of trapdoor made from copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone. A copper trapdoor can exist in one of eight variants depending on how oxidized it is and whether it is waxed or not.
entities.name: Weathered Copper Trapdoor

entities.blurb: Cut copper is an oxidizing metal block crafted from blocks of copper. Like other copper blocks, cut copper can be waxed to prevent oxidation.
entities.name: Weathered Cut Copper

entities.blurb: A cut copper slab is a decorative slab variant of cut copper that generates in trial chambers and is used for building. Unlike other types of slabs, cut copper slabs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Weathered Cut Copper Slab

entities.blurb: Cut copper stairs are a decorative stairs variant of cut copper that generate in trial chambers and are used for building. Unlike other types of stairs, cut copper stairs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Weathered Cut Copper Stairs

entities.blurb: A lightning rod is a block that, with sky access, causes natural lightning strikes in a large area to only target itself. Getting struck by lightning causes it to emit a redstone signal and, if it is not waxed, also reduces its level of oxidation.
entities.name: Weathered Lightning Rod

entities.blurb: Weeping vines are climbable, downwards-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in crimson forests.
entities.name: Weeping Vines

entities.blurb: Weeping vines are climbable, downwards-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in crimson forests.
entities.name: Weeping Vines Plant

entities.blurb: A sponge is a block that can be placed to remove water in an area around itself. This turns it into a wet sponge, which can be smelted or placed in the Nether to dry it to be reused. Sponges can only be found in ocean monuments.
entities.name: Wet Sponge

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: White Banner

entities.blurb: A bed is a dyeable utility block that allows a player in the Overworld to sleep through the night and change their spawn point to within a few blocks of the bed, as long as it is not broken or obstructed. Villagers sleep in beds at night and require spare beds to produce offspring.
entities.name: White Bed

entities.blurb:
A candle is a dyable block that emits light when lit with a flint and steel. Up to four of the same color of candle can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced.
Dyed candles are the dyed variants of candles that come in all sixteen colors. Once dyed, they cannot be changed into a different color.
entities.name: White Candle

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake with White Candle

entities.blurb: Carpets are thin variants of wool that can be dyed in any of the 16 colors.
entities.name: White Carpet

entities.blurb: Concrete is a block created when concrete powder touches water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: White Concrete

entities.blurb: Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block that is converted to concrete when touching water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: White Concrete Powder

entities.blurb: Glazed terracotta is a vibrant solid block that comes in the sixteen regular dye colors, obtained by smelting stained terracotta. Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime blocks or honey blocks, and it cannot be pulled by sticky pistons, but it can be pushed by pistons.
entities.name: White Glazed Terracotta

entities.blurb: A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.
entities.name: White Shulker Box

entities.blurb: Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
entities.name: White Stained Glass

entities.blurb: A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.
entities.name: White Stained Glass Pane

entities.blurb: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
entities.name: White Terracotta

entities.blurb: Flowers are plants that occur in a variety of shapes and colors. Many of them can be crafted into various types of dye and/or suspicious stew, and some have unique properties. Bees collect nectar from most flower types, which they use to fill their home nests and hives with honey. Additionally, most flower types can be used to breed bees.
entities.name: White Tulip

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: White Wall Banner

entities.blurb: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
entities.name: White Wool

entities.blurb: Wildflowers are a thin decorative flower that can be placed four times in the space of one block, similar to pink petals and leaf litter.
entities.name: Wildflowers

entities.blurb: A wither rose is a flower that inflicts the Wither effect on players and mobs that touch it. It drops when a mob or player is killed by a wither.
entities.name: Wither Rose

entities.blurb: A wither skeleton skull is the head of a wither skeleton in the form of a block, which is a rare drop from killed wither skeletons. Three of them can be used to summon a wither, a destructive boss mob that is the only source of Nether stars.
entities.name: Wither Skeleton Skull

entities.blurb: Heads (including skulls) are a group of 7  blocks based on the heads of players and 6 different mobs. All heads can be worn as helmets and serve as special note block instruments.
entities.name: Wither Skeleton Wall Skull
